newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products boosted by crude ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products boosted by crude ahead of holiday.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were boosted by better crude and futures on Wednesday with business thinning out ahead of the end-week holiday, traders said.
Naphtha ended up a notional $2 at $177/$179 cif, tracking gains in NWE where higher gasoline prices have boosted demand for the heavier naphthenic and aromatic grades, traders said.
Gasoline prices finished unchanged but traders said U.S. demand for cat gas underpinned a generally solid market.
"For the first half of May we see the market pretty balanced," one source said. "A lot of cargoes were placed intra-Med and Turkey even after its tender is still looking."
The source said Romania may also look to sell cat gas.
Gas oil length was more evident, but prices rose $2-$3 a tonne because of strength in futures and NWE physical numbers.
Traders said business was not significantly active and the widespread continental European holidays on Thursday were likely to limit business for the rest of the week.
Italian 0.2 pct was pegged at high fob quotes +$3-3.50, but 1.0 and 0.5 pct was more in demand.
EN590 was fairly well supplied with 2-3 cargoes still available with prices assessed around high fob EN590 quotes +$3.

Low sulphur cargo markets were as usual driven out of north-west Europe, with a trader heard picking up cargoes for needs into Israel and possibly Italy, while the dominant Italian purchaser also bought a cargo.
A bunker requirment into Gibraltar was filled by a trader with standard spec Bilbao barrels at a fob price heard to be fob high +$1 to +$1.50.
However other bunker needs appeared to become less urgent, with at least one other potential buyer preferring to wait until after the long weekend in the hope offer levels will come down.
